sample_size.excerpt: The association of body size, lifestyle, and medical conditions with renal cell cancer risk was examined among 161,126 Hawaii-Los Angeles Multiethnic Cohort participants (1993-2002). After 8.3 years of follow-up, 347 renal cell cancer cases (220 men, 127 women) were identified.

cases.excerpt: After 8.3 years of follow-up, 347 renal cell cancer cases (220 men, 127 women) were identified.

effect_size.excerpt: Compared with nondrinkers, men who drank >or=1 drinks/day had a 31% lower risk (95% CI: 0.49, 0.96).

confidence_interval.excerpt: Compared with nondrinkers, men who drank >or=1 drinks/day had a 31% lower risk (95% CI: 0.49, 0.96).

validated_results.title: Polymorphisms of the DNA gene XPD and risk of bladder cancer in a Southeastern Chinese population.
validated_results.reason: Population-based case-control study of newly diagnosed bladder cancer reports alcohol intake as a protective factor for bladder cancer development, though no alcohol-specific effect estimate is given in the abstract.

sample_size.excerpt: In a population-based case-control study, 215 patients with newly diagnosed bladder transitional cell carcinoma and 245 cancer-free controls/healthy subjects (frequency-matched by the age and sex) were genotyped.
